bands.label: Developing
bands.blurb: Real signal across most facets with visible, nameable gaps.

providers.name: AMCS Group
providers.description: AMCS Group is an enterprise cloud software provider for the waste, recycling, resource and transport industries, headquartered in Ireland and backed by Insight Partners. Its flagship AMCS Platform exposes a REST API spanning Core, ERP Platform, Pay, Scale, TLV and Vision AI services, covering directory, accounting, transport, fleet, municipal and weighbridge operations. The API authenticates with a Personal Access Token exchanged for a session cookie, ships Swagger documentation, a hosted sandbox, a Node.js reference client, a Terraform provider, and an API Accelerator Program with pre-coded, MIT-licensed integration templates covering most of a typical integration project.

bands.label: Thin
bands.blurb: Limited machine-readable signal beyond documentation a human can read.

providers.name: Waste Management
providers.description: Waste Management (WM) is the largest environmental services company in North America, providing waste collection, transfer, disposal, and recycling services to over 20 million residential, commercial, industrial, and municipal customers across the United States. WM provides RESTful APIs for customers and third-party integrators to access account data including balance, services, invoices, pickup schedules, and ETAs via JWT authentication.

providers.name: WM
providers.description: WM (formerly Waste Management, Inc.) is North America's largest integrated environmental solutions company, serving nearly 20 million municipal, commercial, industrial, and residential customers through collection, transfer, recycling, landfill, and waste-to-energy operations. WM does not run a self-serve, publicly-signup developer platform. It publishes a documented partner/customer REST API at api.wm.com covering account-level service and billing data - service details and pickup schedules, live service status and truck ETA, routing and hauling material information, pricing, invoices and aging balance, communication preferences, contacts, cases, tickets, and account activity notes. Access requires a WM-issued ClientId plus a JSON Web Token (JWT) and is granted on request to existing commercial/enterprise customers and integration partners by emailing apiaccess@wm.com; there is no open, self-serve API key signup.

bands.label: Emerging
bands.blurb: More than an index entry but still mostly links rather than artifacts.

providers.name: Waste Connections
providers.description: Waste Connections is the third-largest integrated provider of solid waste services in North America, serving approximately nine million residential, commercial, and industrial customers across 46 U.S. states and six Canadian provinces. The company provides non-hazardous waste collection, transfer, disposal, and recycling services, primarily in exclusive and secondary markets. Waste Connections is investing in AI-powered dynamic routing and expanding customer connectivity features through its online customer portal.

providers.name: Stericycle
providers.description: Stericycle is a Fortune 500 compliance company specializing in regulated medical waste disposal, sharps management, pharmaceutical waste, secure information destruction, and healthcare compliance training. In November 2024, Stericycle was acquired by Waste Management (WM) for approximately $7.2 billion. The company operates as WM Healthcare Solutions division, serving hospitals, clinics, medical offices, dental practices, veterinary facilities, and other healthcare organizations. Stericycle's MyStericycle customer portal enables online account management, scheduling, compliance training, and billing.

providers.name: Goodr
providers.description: Goodr is an Atlanta-based sustainable surplus food management and hunger-relief logistics company founded in 2016 by Jasmine Crowe-Houston. Goodr helps businesses divert edible and inedible food waste from landfills by scheduling pickups, donating surplus edible food to local nonprofits, and providing donors with the tax deductions and impact reporting tied to those donations. Alongside its food-waste solutions, Goodr runs hunger-relief programs including pop-up grocery markets, meal delivery, student snackpacks, and community grocery stores. The company reports more than 30 million meals served and 4 million pounds of food diverted from landfills for enterprise partners such as Amazon, Google, NASA, and Fulton County. Goodr operates through a partner portal rather than a public developer API; this profile tracks its public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Resourcify
providers.description: Resourcify (Resourcify GmbH) is a Hamburg, Germany based digital platform for waste management and circular-economy operations, describing itself as "the operating system for a circular future." Its cloud software helps enterprises digitize and optimize their waste streams end to end - automating waste and recycling operations, optimizing cost, CO2 and recycling rates, tracking compliance, and running take-back systems - across manufacturing, construction, retail, healthcare, and airports. The platform connects waste producers with a network of recyclers and haulers, captures waste data and documentation, and reports on sustainability and material recovery. Resourcify is backed by Speedinvest. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal; integrations are delivered as managed connections rather than a self-serve API.

providers.name: Junk King
providers.description: Junk King is a professional junk removal and hauling franchise operating across the United States and Canada as part of the Neighborly family of home service brands. Through locally owned and operated locations, Junk King provides full-service junk removal, self-service dumpster rental, and dumpster bag pickup for residential and commercial customers, handling appliance and furniture removal, estate and property cleanouts, construction debris, yard waste, and e-waste. The company emphasizes eco-friendly disposal, recycling, donating, and reusing as much collected material as possible. Junk King offers free estimates, same-day service in many markets, and online, phone, and text-based booking. It is a portfolio company associated with Norwest Venture Partners and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; Junk King publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Clean Harbors
providers.description: Clean Harbors is the largest provider of environmental and industrial services in North America, delivering hazardous and non-hazardous waste management, emergency response, industrial cleaning, environmental remediation, and used-oil and solvent recycling through its Safety-Kleen subsidiary. Clean Harbors does not publish a public developer portal or general-purpose REST API surface; programmatic interfaces are limited to the authenticated customer portal at clhsaas.cleanharbors.com (CLH SaaS) for service requests, manifests, and reporting, and partner-mediated EDI feeds. Customers also use the EPA e-Manifest system for federally regulated hazardous-waste manifest tracking.

providers.name: Greyparrot
providers.description: Greyparrot is a London-based AI waste analytics company that turns materials recovery facilities (MRFs) into data-driven operations. Its Greyparrot Analyzer uses computer-vision cameras mounted over waste conveyor belts to identify, count, and measure the composition of waste streams in real time, giving recyclers continuous visibility into what flows through their plant. The Greyparrot Sync product routes that analytics stream into existing operational control systems, ERP platforms, Power BI dashboards, and OEM sortation hardware (robotic arms, air-jet systems, balers, belt control), while Deepnest turns real-world recovery data into design feedback for packaging brands. Backed by Speedinvest, Greyparrot serves recyclers, equipment manufacturers, and consumer-goods companies working to raise recycling rates and automate compliance reporting. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition; this profile captures its public web, product, and content surface.

providers.name: AMP Robotics
providers.description: AMP Robotics (operating as AMP Sortation) is an artificial-intelligence company for the waste and recycling industry that designs, builds, and operates advanced, cost-competitive facilities to process single-stream recycling and municipal solid waste. Its Smart Sortation technology suite combines computer vision (real-time material characterization), high-speed air-jet sortation (Jet and MicroJet), and robotic-arm sortation (Delta) to raise material-recovery rates, cut contamination, and extend landfill life. The flagship AMP ONE platform delivers fully automated, facility-scale sortation processing from 10K to 1M+ tons annually for waste haulers, material-recovery facilities, and municipalities. AMP Robotics is a Google Ventures (GV) portfolio company. No public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal is published; this profile is maintained for network discovery and identity.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Recycleye
providers.description: Recycleye is a London-based company building AI-powered sorting equipment and analytics for waste management and material recovery businesses worldwide. Its products include Recycleye QualiBot robotic sorting cells, Recycleye QuantiSort optical sorting technology, and Recycleye Insights, a data analytics platform that uses computer vision (WasteNet) to identify and categorize waste streams. The company sells hardware and software into recycling operations to improve purity, recovery rates, and profitability. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC. As of this enrichment pass Recycleye publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: Resynergi
providers.description: Resynergi is an advanced plastic recycling technology company that builds modular Continuous Microwave Assisted Pyrolysis (CMAP) systems, marketed as AMP Modules, which convert hard-to-recycle waste plastics (HDPE, LDPE, polypropylene and polystyrene) into circular pyrolysis oil (PyOil) and other petrochemical feedstocks. Each 440 sq ft module is designed to process roughly 5 tons of plastic waste per day and produce about 1,000 gallons of PyOil per day, and the company claims a conversion roughly twenty times faster than conventional pyrolysis with a large reduction in CO2-equivalent emissions. Founded in 2015 by Jason Tanne and Brian Bauer around microwave pyrolysis research from the University of Minnesota, Resynergi commercializes its modules in partnership with Lummus Technology, which sells the AMP Modules, and also operates plants near the source of waste under a partner model. This is an industrial process-equipment business; it is not a software vendor and publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Blau Corp
providers.description: Blau (Blau Corp) is a waste-management operating system for haulers (gestores), final-destination facilities, and government regulators across Mexico, Colombia, and Spain. The SaaS platform delivers AI-assisted route optimization, route-level profitability analysis, automated RP and RPBI hazardous- and biological-infectious-waste manifests, online collection booking, and end-to-end traceability, plus the Blau Driver mobile app for field crews. Founded in Guadalajara, Mexico in 2021 and backed by 500 Global (LatAm B17 batch), Blau integrates with SAT/CFDI, SEMARNAT, SAP/ERP, QuickBooks, WhatsApp, fleet GPS, and Power BI. Blau does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: SolarCycle
providers.description: SolarCycle is a technology-driven solar recycling company founded in 2022 that provides certified end-of-life management for solar energy systems. It recovers up to 97% of panel materials (silver, copper, gold, aluminum, glass), recycles power electronics such as inverters and transformers, and handles logistics and field operations for large-scale solar projects, achieving 100% landfill diversion. SolarCycle operates seven facilities across Georgia, Illinois, Texas, Nevada, and Arizona and is building a domestic recycled-solar-glass manufacturing plant, serving major solar companies including Q Cells, AES, Orsted, and Sunrun. It is a portfolio company of Fifth Wall. This is a physical circular-economy operations business with no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Fazla Gida
providers.description: Fazla (formerly Fazla Gida / Whole Surplus) is a Turkish technology-driven waste management and circular-economy company founded in 2017 in Istanbul. Its digital, decision-support platform helps B2B clients across the supply chain — manufacturers, retailers, e-commerce, distributors, HoReCa, food banks and municipalities — prevent waste at the source and recover value from surplus inventory through a food-recovery hierarchy of secondary-sales marketplace, donation, animal-feed conversion and recycling modules, backed by logistics support, a smart-scale IoT inventory system and an AI analysis tool that reports financial, CO2 and social impact. The company operates the Fazla Iyi surprise-box consumer app, is the first B Corp-certified waste-management organization in Turkey, and is backed by 500 Global among other investors.

providers.name: Evreka
providers.description: Evreka is a smart waste and recycling management technology company offering an end-to-end "Sustainability as a Service" platform that digitizes the entire waste management lifecycle. Its software suite spans operations, fleet, asset, MRF, and workforce management, route optimization, citizen engagement, and EPR/PRO management, complemented by IoT hardware such as fill-level sensors, vehicle and container trackers, and RFID readers. Evreka serves dumpster rental, recycling centers, medical, hazardous and liquid waste, construction and demolition, local authorities, and cross-border waste operators. Backed by 500 Global, it is tracked in the API Evangelist network; no public API or developer portal is currently published.

providers.name: EverestLabs
providers.description: EverestLabs builds AI, computer vision, and robotics for the recycling industry. Its RecycleOS platform identifies, tracks, and sorts recoverable materials on the conveyor lines of Materials Recovery Facilities (MRFs), giving recyclers, reclaimers, and packaging manufacturers analytics, bale tracing, plant optimization, and compliance reporting to increase recovery rates, cut labor costs, and verify recycled content. Headquartered in Fremont, California and backed by Sierra Ventures. EverestLabs does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, GitHub, and discovery surface.

providers.name: Entocycle
providers.description: Entocycle is a London-based insect farming technology company building industrial-scale, controlled-environment facilities that use black soldier fly bioconversion to turn organic waste streams into insect protein for animal feed and organic fertilizer (frass). Its platform combines modular climate-controlled farm infrastructure, real-time AI-driven insect monitoring that counts and tracks insects across their lifecycle, and fully automated production systems to standardize output across deployments worldwide. Entocycle partners with waste management companies, agricultural producers, insect companies, and offtake buyers to develop and operate circular-economy insect farms. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Dayjob
providers.description: Dayjob is an AI-powered scheduling agent built for waste management and skip hire fleets, operated by Gaea Technology Ltd and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026). Its autonomous agents analyze millions of potential route combinations to build optimized daily schedules that factor in travel times, skip sizes, driver availability and priority job assignments, then continuously re-optimize in real time as new jobs, driver changes and exceptions arrive. Dayjob integrates with existing ERP and telematics systems (Weighsoft, PurGo, Wastelogics, plus custom report setups) and claims customers see revenue and efficiency gains, tighter time-window hit rates and materially less planning admin. It is a vertical logistics application rather than an API platform - no public developer portal, API reference or SDKs are published at this time. This profile has been enriched from the company's public website.

providers.name: Republic Services
providers.description: Republic Services is one of the largest providers of non-hazardous solid waste disposal, recycling, and environmental services in the United States. As a Fortune 500 company, Republic Services serves millions of customers across residential, commercial, industrial, and environmental segments. The company offers waste collection, recycling processing, composting, landfill operations, and digital customer tools for account management, service scheduling, and environmental reporting.

providers.name: Vaulted Deep
providers.description: Vaulted Deep is a permanent carbon removal and organic waste disposal company that injects carbon-filled organic waste — biosolids, agricultural byproducts and manure, and pulp and paper sludge — thousands of feet underground as a slurry, using patented geologic slurry sequestration technology adapted from oil and gas practice so the carbon is trapped permanently beneath impermeable rock. Spun out of Advantek Waste Management Services in 2023 and co-founded by Julia Reichelstein and Omar Abou-Sayed, it operates the Great Plains site in Hutchinson, Kansas and the Terminal Island site in Los Angeles, California, serving municipal wastewater utilities and agricultural operators while selling durable carbon removal credits to corporate buyers. It publishes no public API, SDK, or developer program.

providers.name: Dimension
providers.description: Dimension is a nationwide, on-demand waste management and junk removal platform (formerly Trash Warrior) backed by 500 Global. It offers digital booking with instant AI-generated pricing (their "Mirror Mirror AI" quoter), same-day and next-day pickup for cardboard, appliances, mattresses, hazardous and medical waste, plus dumpster rentals, for both businesses and individuals. Every job includes tracking with detailed diversion data, receipts, and photos, and can be booked as a one-off or recurring service. Dimension has been awarded a State of California RFP contract for PPE waste removal. The company operates a customer-facing booking application and help center but does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Whole Surplus
providers.description: Whole Surplus (now operating as Fazla) is a Turkish technology-based waste management and circular-economy company backed by Techstars. It prevents waste at its source and recovers surplus products back into the circular economy with maximum environmental, social, and economic benefit across the entire supply chain from producers to consumers. Its platform combines an AI-powered analysis tool that identifies the optimal recovery path for each product with services including Fazla Market (discounted resale), donations to food banks, animal-feed conversion, recycling, a smart-scale detection system, and sustainability consultancy. Fazla is the first B Corp certified waste-management company in Turkey and is supported by the UN Development Programme (UNDP). The company operates a customer web application (app.fazla.com) but publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specification at this time.

providers.name: GreenQ
providers.description: GreenQ is an Israeli smart waste-management technology company (founded 2015, Jerusalem) promoting the "Internet of Garbage" — turning ordinary garbage trucks into smart trucks. Its GreenTrack device installs on any collection vehicle to weigh incoming waste and track route, mileage, capacity, time and per-bin (single-can-level) pickup data without requiring sensors on the bins, using a patent-pending visual-recognition algorithm. A recommendations engine then suggests route-optimization and scheduling improvements, surfaced through the GreenQ dashboard of reports and analytics. Collected data can be integrated with a municipality's local-authority systems through a private integration API; the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or specification. GreenQ was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global (also backed by URBAN-X) and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Rubicon
providers.description: Rubicon (formerly NYSE: RBT) is a waste, recycling, and sustainability technology company founded in 2008. It went public in 2022 via a SPAC merger with Founder SPAC at a pro forma valuation of roughly $1.7 billion, branding itself a "digital challenger" to the traditional waste-hauling industry with a marketplace connecting waste generators to independent haulers plus the RUBICONSmartCity fleet-and-routing platform used by more than 70 municipalities. Operating Status: the company subsequently faced severe financial distress - layoffs and debt restructuring in 2023, a June 2024 NYSE delisting, and a May 2024 divestiture of its entire fleet technology and smart-city business unit (RUBICONSmartCity, RUBICONPro, RUBICONPremier) to Rodina Capital for roughly $68 million plus a possible $12 million earnout; those assets were subsequently absorbed by Routeware. In early 2025 Rubicon deregistered its securities and became a privately held company, majority-owned by Jose Miguel Enrich through MBI Holdings, and remains the subject of shareholder litigation over the change-of-control terms. The surviving company operates as a smaller enterprise waste brokerage and sustainability-data business built around the RUBICONConnect platform (service, equipment, pickup, and cost visibility for enterprise customers such as Chipotle and FedEx), alongside RUBICONRegWatch compliance tooling, sustainability reporting, technical advisory services, and the Rubicon Now on-demand dumpster-rental service in a handful of cities. rubicon.com publishes no developer portal, no public API reference, and no OpenAPI specification. The only discoverable API artifact tied to the rubicon.com domain is a "Routeware Smartcity Public Api" Swagger UI hosted at a dev subdomain (haulerpublic-api.dev.aws.rubicon.com) - leftover infrastructure from the divested fleet/smart-city business - which returned a 503 Service Unavailable on every check during this review and is not publicly documented or reachable. Any hauler or municipal system integration Rubicon references (for example, connecting to city 311 systems) is negotiated per partner and gated behind sales and onboarding rather than exposed through self-serve developer documentation. Pricing across RUBICONConnect and Rubicon's enterprise services is entirely quote-based and negotiated per contract; no public pricing, tiers, or rate limits are published. This entry is maintained as an honest stub pending any future public API surface.

providers.name: Schuettflix
providers.description: Schuettflix is a German digital logistics platform for the construction industry, founded in 2018 in Guetersloh. It operates a neutral B2B marketplace that connects construction companies, bulk-material suppliers, freight forwarders and waste-disposal firms in a single fully digital workflow. Through its iOS and Android apps, customers order sand, gravel and crushed stone with transparent real-time pricing, coordinate dispatch and transport, capture delivery documentation, manage routes, and handle mineral-waste disposal and circular-economy recycling of construction materials. The company digitizes the traditionally analog and fragmented process of procuring and delivering bulk goods, earning a commission on the transactions facilitated through its platform. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest. No public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Roadrunner
providers.description: RoadRunner is a tech-enabled managed waste and recycling services company operating across all 50 US states, serving 14,000+ commercial customers in hospitality, healthcare, retail, logistics and manufacturing. It consolidates multi-location waste programs and layers proprietary optimization tooling (Oversite, Waste Metering, BillCheck, Priceshield) plus the RecycleMORE and CleanStream recycling programs on top of hauler networks. Backed by Fifth Wall and Kleiner Perkins in the climate sector. As of this enrichment pass RoadRunner publishes a marketing site and a customer + payment portal but no public developer/API surface, so no OpenAPI, SDK, MCP or event artifacts were found.

providers.name: Veolia
providers.description: A French multinational corporation and the global leader in environmental services including water management, waste management, and energy services. Operates in nearly 50 countries providing solutions for water treatment, waste recycling, and pollution remediation.

providers.name: Fulcrum BioEnergy
providers.description: Fulcrum BioEnergy, Inc. was a Pleasanton, California waste-to-fuels project developer founded in 2007 that converted municipal solid waste into synthetic crude oil for refining into sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and diesel, using a shred-and-sort feedstock line feeding a gasifier and a Fischer-Tropsch conversion train. Its first and only commercial plant, the Sierra BioFuels Plant in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center outside Reno, Nevada, was designed to take roughly 175,000-219,000 tons of household garbage a year from an adjacent feedstock processing facility and began production in late 2022. The company raised on the order of a billion dollars in equity, debt and government support over its life, including strategic investments and offtake alliances with United Airlines, Waste Management, Cathay Pacific Airways, Marubeni and bp, plus a US Department of Energy loan guarantee, USDA loan guarantee and Department of Defense grants; E. James Macias led it as president and CEO through its build-out years, and it had announced follow-on projects including a Gary, Indiana plant and the NorthPoint facility in the UK. The Sierra plant stopped operating in mid-May 2024 after persistent equipment problems, the company laid off essentially its entire workforce and took its website down, and on 2024-09-09 Fulcrum BioEnergy, Fulcrum Sierra Holdings and Fulcrum Sierra Finance Co. filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware listing more than $456 million owed to over 200 creditors. A November 2024 auction sold the biorefinery to Switch, Ltd. for $55 million and the adjacent feedstock processing facility to Refuse Inc., a WM subsidiary; the plan of liquidation was confirmed in April 2025 and went effective in May 2025. Fulcrum was an industrial energy project developer rather than a software company and never published a developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface, or machine-readable specification — a Wayback index of its corporate site from 2008 through 2024 turns up no developer, reference, or spec path of any kind. Its corporate host fulcrum-bioenergy.com no longer resolves to any web server, and the alternate registration fulcrumbioenergy.com is parked on the GoDaddy/Afternic aftermarket and listed for sale. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.
